stories.title: Masks, test kits back on shopping lists amid signs of Covid-19 resurgence in S. Korea
stories.summary: Covid-19 cases are rising in South Korea, causing increased sales of masks, test kits, and cold medicines at major convenience stores. Sales of masks for children and infants surged by 341%, reflecting concerns among parents and daycare centres. Experts expect demand to stay high due to schools reopening and seasonal changes, with hospitalisations also increasing sharply. As Covid-19 infections begin to climb in South Korea, pandemic-era shopping habits are making a comeback, with people once again reaching for masks and self-test kits. All three major convenience store chains – 7-Eleven, GS25 and CU – have seen a sharp rise in sales of related products over the past month, according to news reports on Aug 28. Sales of Covid-19 self-test kits at 7-Eleven, for example, recorded a 62 per cent on-month rise from Aug 1 to Aug 26, while those of masks, cold medicine and fever and pain relievers rose 17 per cent, 15 per cent and 14 per cent, respectively, data showed. GS25 also reported a 30.3 per cent increase in test kits and a 10.3 per cent gain in cold medicine over the same period. Demand was particularly strong for masks for children and infants, with sales more than quadrupling from the previous month, up 341 per cent, officials said. CU saw a similar trend from Aug 1 to Aug 23, with sales of test kits and cold medicine up 45.7 per cent and 12.2 per cent, respectively, from the same period a month earlier. “Since mid-August, we’ve been asking parents to send their children to day care with masks after a series of cold-like illnesses accompanied by high fevers among 1- and 2-year-olds,” Hwang Ji-mi, a teacher at a day care center in Dongjak-gu, Seoul, told. The Korea Herald. Industry sources say the recent uptick in Covid-19 infections is bringing back the shopping habits that became commonplace during the pandemic.
